summary: Timezone bug on Sanctus daily-practice 'Completed at' timestamp is FIXED and verified. Backend GET /api/daily-practice now returns `completed_at` as an ISO string with `+00:00` UTC offset (e.g. `2026-06-08T21:31:22.312000+00:00`). Frontend DailyPracticeCard renders this with `new Date(iso).toLocaleTimeString(...)` which correctly converts to the browser's local timezone. Verified with Playwright using browser-context `timezone_id` emulation: in America/New_York (UTC-4) the card showed 5:33 PM (matching backend UTC 21:33:26 = local 5:33 PM) and in America/Los_Angeles (UTC-7) it showed 2:33 PM (matching UTC 21:33:39 = local 2:33 PM). Both 0-minute diff vs in-page `new Date().toLocaleTimeString()` captured at moment of click. Pre-fix behavior would have shown 9:33 PM in NY (4h off); that regression is gone.

critical_code_review_comments: _strip() in /app/backend/daily_practices.py:867 now correctly attaches `tzinfo=timezone.utc` to naive datetimes from MongoDB before isoformat(). Comment in source documents the rationale clearly.

Frontend /app/frontend/src/components/DailyPracticeCard.tsx:214 uses `new Date(practice.completed_at).toLocaleTimeString([], {hour:'numeric', minute:'2-digit'})` — this is correct because the backend now always returns an offset-bearing ISO string, so the Date constructor parses it as an absolute instant rather than mistaking it for local time.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Tip: the in-tool browser_automation harness can't always parse f-strings with embedded curly-brace JS-evaluate strings — when in doubt, write a standalone /app/test_reports/<name>.py and run with `python` (playwright installed at /root/.venv). Use `browser.new_context(timezone_id='...')` for clean per-tab TZ emulation rather than CDP override (simpler and equally effective).
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: MongoDB returns naive datetimes (no tzinfo). Previously `_strip` called `v.isoformat()` directly which produced strings like '2026-06-08T21:31:22.312000' with NO offset. JavaScript's `new Date('2026-06-08T21:31:22.312')` on ISO strings without offset is parsed as LOCAL time per ECMA-262, so a US-East user saw 9:31 PM instead of the correct 5:31 PM EDT (4-hour shift). FIX (verified): `_strip` now does `v = v.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` before isoformat when tzinfo is None, producing '2026-06-08T21:31:22.312000+00:00'. JS Date now parses as absolute UTC instant and toLocaleTimeString converts it to the user's actual local timezone. Verified end-to-end across UTC-4 and UTC-7 with 0-minute drift between displayed value and `new Date().toLocaleTimeString()` captured at click time.
